documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 12/28/2025, 18:10.

CC: fever, incision pain.
HPI: 36-year-old woman with Crohn's disease and SLE, postoperative day 3 after emergency cesarean delivery for fetal distress. Pain and redness around the incision since this morning; temperature 38.5 C at home. Breastfeeding.
Meds: mesalamine 1.2 g TID, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol PRN, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. NKDA.

Vitals: T 38.5 C; remaining vital signs within normal limits. BMI 34.
Exam: Low transverse cesarean incision with surrounding erythema and induration and a small amount of purulent drainage; no foul odor. No fluctuance. No crepitus. Abdomen otherwise soft. Fundus firm, appropriately tender. Breasts without erythema.

Labs: WBC 14.0, CRP 86 mg/L.
Wound culture sent.

Assessment: superficial incisional surgical site infection (cellulitis) after cesarean.
Plan: cephalexin 500 mg PO four times daily for 7 days. Wound care instructions. Follow-up with OB tomorrow as scheduled. Return for spreading redness, worsening pain or persistent fever.

documents.title: Obstetrics postpartum visit, day 4
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside OB/MFM group. Date of service 12/29/2025.

Postpartum day 4 after emergency cesarean. Seen in ED yesterday for incisional cellulitis, on cephalexin; afebrile today.
Complaint: both breasts painful and swollen. Trying to breastfeed; baby not latching well and she worries the baby isn't getting enough. No fever today, no nipple discharge, no red streaking.
Vitals within normal limits.
Exam: breasts symmetrically enlarged, firm, tender. No skin color change. Nipples intact without cracks or fissures. No palpable axillary nodes. Incision: erythema receding, no drainage.
Assessment: postpartum breast engorgement. Mild incisional cellulitis improving.
Plan: feed or express every 2-3 hours, warm compress before and cold after feeds, gentle hand expression to soften before latch, same-day lactation consultant visit. Finish cephalexin. Postpartum visit at 4 weeks.

documents.title: Obstetrics postpartum visit, 4 weeks
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside OB/MFM group. Date of service 01/22/2026.

Routine 4-week postpartum visit; infant along, well and gaining weight. Exclusively breastfeeding. Two days of painful blisters on the right breast. No fever, chills or flu-like illness. No recent vaccines, no sick contacts. Engorgement resolved.
Vitals within normal limits.
Exam: grouped vesicles on an erythematous base confined to the right areola. No similar lesions elsewhere. Incision healed.
Labs: HIV antibody negative. CBC within normal limits. RPR nonreactive.
Assessment: herpes simplex infection of the right areola.
Plan: valacyclovir 1 g twice daily for 7 days. Breastfeed from the left; pump and discard from the right until all lesions are crusted. Hand hygiene. Return as needed.

Medications listed: mesalamine, hydroxychloroquine, prednisone 10 mg, albuterol, ferrous sulfate. NKDA.

events.reason: ED record and discharge summary received

reports.text: Noncontrast CT head. Hemorrhagic lesion in the left parietal lobe with surrounding vasogenic edema. No midline shift. No hydrocephalus. No other intracranial hemorrhage. Calvarium intact.
CT angiogram of the chest. No pulmonary embolism. Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Heart size normal. No mediastinal adenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules. No pulmonary embolism.

reports.study: MRI brain without and with contrast
reports.text: Single 2.1 cm enhancing hemorrhagic lesion in the left parietal lobe with surrounding edema and mild local mass effect. No additional lesions. No vascular malformation. Ventricles normal.
reports.conclusion: Solitary hemorrhagic left parietal metastasis, 2.1 cm.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 07/01/2026, 13:30. Stroke alert.

HPI: 36-year-old woman, about six months after delivery, with SLE, Crohn's disease, HHT and choriocarcinoma treated in 2024. Abrupt right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking this afternoon. In recent weeks she had spells of lightheadedness and an intermittent dull chest discomfort she had not mentioned to anyone. No follow-up care since her postpartum visit. No hypertension, diabetes or prior stroke. No drug use, recent travel or trauma.
Meds: mesalamine, hydroxychloroquine, prednisone 10 mg, albuterol PRN, ferrous sulfate. NKDA.

Vitals: T 37.1 C (98.8 F), BP 118/76, HR 92.
Exam: awake and alert. Expressive aphasia. Right facial droop. Right arm and leg weakness. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.

Labs: Hgb 10.8, WBC 7.9, platelets 242. Serum beta-hCG 75,300 mIU/mL.
CT head: hemorrhagic left parietal lesion. CTA chest: multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, no PE.
Not a thrombolysis candidate (hemorrhage).

Assessment: hemorrhagic brain lesion with lung nodules and high hCG after a term pregnancy, in a patient with prior choriocarcinoma - metastatic gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. Admitted; gyn onc and neurosurgery consulted.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Regional hospital - Gynecologic Oncology. Admitted 07/01/2026, discharged 07/11/2026.

Diagnosis: choriocarcinoma metastatic to brain and lungs, presenting six months after a term cesarean delivery; prior post-abortal choriocarcinoma 2024 treated to remission. FIGO stage IV, prognostic score 15 (ultra-high risk).

Course: MRI brain 7/2: single 2.1 cm hemorrhagic enhancing left parietal metastasis with edema, no other lesions. Dexamethasone 4 mg IV every 6 hours. Levetiracetam continued; no seizures. Neurosurgery: no operation at present. Low-dose etoposide-cisplatin induction started 07/03 to lower the risk of tumor bleeding; EP/EMA with high-dose methotrexate for CNS disease to begin 07/17 at the cancer center. Breastfeeding stopped. PT, OT and speech therapy daily: right arm and leg strength improving, speech improving.

Discharge exam: mild expressive word-finding difficulty, right grip 4/5, right leg 4+/5, walking without device.

Discharge medications: dexamethasone 2 mg PO BID with taper per oncology; levetiracetam 500 mg BID; hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily; prednisone 10 mg daily; mesalamine 1.2 g TID; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily; albuterol PRN.

Follow-up: cancer center 07/17 to begin EP/EMA; hCG every 2 weeks with cycles; outpatient PT, OT and speech therapy referrals placed; PCP within 1 week. No driving.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology progress letter
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Cancer center - gynecologic oncology. Visit 08/11/2026.
Choriocarcinoma, FIGO IV:15, on EP/EMA with high-dose methotrexate since 07/17 after etoposide-cisplatin induction. hCG 75,300 (7/1), 41,200 (7/14), 6,880 (7/28), 1,124 (8/11) - responding. No new neurological symptoms; speech and right-sided strength improving with therapy. Dexamethasone taper completed 08/07. Continue EP/EMA, hCG with each cycle. Radiation oncology opinion on the brain lesion to be revisited once hCG is normal.
